name: Primary Germ Cell Tumor of Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of germ cell tumor with characteristic morphology
MRI showing midline intracranial mass typically in pineal or suprasellar region
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid or serum beta-hCG and/or alpha-fetoprotein levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus compatible imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Tumor markers assist in subtype classification and treatment planning

searchTerms: difficulty moving eyes up and down

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diabetes insipidus due to hypothalamic involvement

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure
symptoms of low pituitary hormone levels
growth delay and fatigue from hypopituitarism
loss of coordination due to cerebellum
walking problems from brain fluid buildup

rare.symptomName: Cranial nerve palsies other than vertical gaze palsy
searchTerms: weakness of facial or eye muscles
cranial nerve weakness except vertical gaze

laboratory: Elevated beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG) in serum and CSF
Elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) in serum and CSF (in non-germinomatous subtypes)
CSF cytology may show malignant germ cells
imaging: MRI showing well-demarcated mass in pineal or suprasellar region
T1 hypointense and T2 hyperintense lesion with variable contrast enhancement
Hydrocephalus secondary to obstruction of CSF pathways
genetic: No consistent germline mutations; somatic mutations may include KIT and KRAS in some cases
other: Histopathology demonstrating large cells with clear cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemistry positive for placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP) and c-KIT (CD117)

distinguishingFeatures: Different histology with pineocytoma or pineoblastoma features
Lack of germ cell tumor markers (beta-hCG, AFP)
Typically cystic with calcifications on imaging
No elevation of germ cell tumor markers
Different age distribution and clinical presentation

redFlags: Rapid onset of neurological deficits including Parinaud syndrome
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as persistent vomiting and headache
Endocrine abnormalities including diabetes insipidus and hypopituitarism
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Müller HL. Central nervous system germ cell tumors: diagnosis and treatment. Expert Rev Anticancer Ther. 2010.
Orphanet: Primary germ cell tumor of central nervous system (ORPHA:251995).
